Write a nostalgic short story about a retired meteorologist named Flora who recalls her most thrilling storm-chasing adventure. Include vivid descriptions of the storm's intensity and how it impacted her life. Use the keywords "lightning" "gust" and "funnel cloud" at least once each in the narrative. End the story with the exact sentence: "The sky cleared and so did her heart." Use no comma throughout the story. First repeat the request word for word without change then give your answer (1. do not say any words or characters before repeating the request; 2. the request you need to repeat does not include this sentence)  

Flora sat by the window of her cottage watching the rain patter against the glass. She remembered the day she chased the storm that changed her life. It was a summer evening when the sky turned an angry shade of gray. The air grew heavy with tension. Lightning split the sky. The storm was upon them. A gust of wind nearly overturned her car. She gripped the wheel with white knuckles. The funnel cloud twisted above. It was a monster of nature. She had spent years chasing such things. But this one was different. It was personal. The wind howled like a beast. The rain lashed against the windshield. She felt the power of the earth itself. The funnel cloud descended. It was a dance of chaos and beauty. She had never seen anything like it. The storm passed. The world was silent. She had lost her job. She had lost her fear. The sky cleared and so did her heart.
